skills.name: nci-startup
skills.title: NCI Startup
skills.description: Use this skill when you are beginning a piece of work at NCI and do not yet know which NCI skills apply. It helps technical staff who do not write code choose, download, and set up the right skills from the NCI Skills Library, and check that their computer has the tools those skills need. Produces an installed set of skills, a tool readiness report, and a plain-English summary of what happened and what to do next.

skills.name: code-scanning-report
skills.title: Code Scanning Alert Analysis & Report
skills.description: Analyze GitHub Code Scanning (SAST) alerts for a GitHub repository and generate a comprehensive report with severity breakdowns, rule/CWE mappings, affected source files with line numbers, and per-rule remediation guidance. Requires gh CLI (preferred) or GITHUB_TOKEN. Uses gh api with --paginate and a state=open filter for reliable, complete data retrieval.

skills.title: Dependabot Alert Analysis & Upgrade Report
skills.description: Analyze GitHub Dependabot security alerts for a GitHub repository and generate a comprehensive upgrade report with breaking changes, effort estimates, and recommended versions. Requires gh CLI (preferred) or GITHUB_TOKEN. Uses gh api with --paginate and a state=open filter for reliable, complete data retrieval.

skills.name: book-summary
skills.title: Book Summary Skill
skills.description: Produces a comprehensive summary of a book to help the user decide whether to read it and how to use it. Use this skill whenever the user uploads or references a book (any genre or format) and asks to "summarize it", "give me a summary", "what is this book about", "should I read this", "is this worth reading", "give me the gist", "distill this for me", or "what does this cover". Also trigger when the user says "help me decide if I should read X" or "overview of X." The output is a rich Markdown summary report tailored to the book's type — enough to make an informed read-or-skip decision. Always use this skill for these requests — do not substitute a short, conversational summary.

skills.name: c4-analysis
skills.title: C4 Analysis Skill
skills.description: Reverse-engineers a C4 architecture model from an existing codebase and produces Mermaid.js diagrams (Context, Container, Component, and optionally Code-level) plus supporting Markdown documentation. Use this skill whenever the user wants to understand the current architecture of a project, asks to "C4 model this codebase", "diagram the architecture", "map out the system", or is preparing for a refactoring effort and needs a baseline architectural view. Always trigger this skill before any DDD analysis or refactoring planning skill — it provides the structural foundation everything else builds on. Also use when user says things like "what does this system look like architecturally" or "help me understand this codebase at a high level."

skills.name: code-review
skills.title: Code Review Skill
skills.description: Performs a thorough, structured code review of a codebase, branch, set of changes, or specific files. Use this skill whenever the user asks for a code review, PR review, diff review, or asks you to "review" any code — whether it's a full repo, a recent commit, a feature branch, or a single file. Produces a categorized, severity-tagged issue report covering correctness, security, performance, architecture, readability, error handling, testing, and documentation. Supports multi-language codebases with separate report sections per language. Always trigger this skill for review requests, even if the user's phrasing is casual ("can you look at this?", "what do you think of this code?").

skills.name: codebase-orientation
skills.title: Codebase Orientation Skill
skills.description: Explores an unfamiliar or legacy codebase and produces a structured orientation report covering entry points, architecture, key components, data models, configuration, workflows, and external dependencies. Use this skill whenever the user is new to a codebase, asks to "understand", "explore", "orient", "map out", "get familiar with", or "figure out how" a project works — even if they don't use the word "orientation". Also trigger when the user says things like "I inherited this project", "I need to get up to speed on this", "what does this codebase do", "where do I start", or "walk me through this code". Always use this skill for these requests — do not just summarize files conversationally.

skills.name: ddd-analysis
skills.title: DDD Analysis Skill
skills.description: Performs a Domain-Driven Design (DDD) analysis of a codebase and maps its concepts to DDD elements: subdomains (core/supporting/generic), bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, aggregates, entities, value objects, domain events, repositories, services, and context map integration patterns. Produces a Markdown document with supporting Mermaid.js diagrams. Use this skill whenever the user wants to apply DDD to an existing codebase, asks to "identify bounded contexts", "map the domain", "find aggregates", "analyze the domain model", "do a DDD analysis", or is preparing to refactor a project toward a cleaner architecture. Always use this skill after c4-analysis (if available) and before refactoring-plan. Also trigger when user says "what's the domain model here" or "help me find the business concepts."

skills.name: implementation-report
skills.title: implementation-report
skills.description: Produces a human-readable explanation of a change request (CR) — what was done, why, what was considered, and how the most critical changes work. Not a code review; an implementation narrative for developers, reviewers, and future maintainers. Output is written as implementation-report-<slug>.md.
